clue.text: An old person's island

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an archaic word for a human being or creature
second meaning: the island off England's south coast, across the Solent from Southampton

explanation.surface: An elderly man owns a little island of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possession but is just 'is' joining the two meanings. The Isle of Wight lies off Hampshire in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wight is an archaic noun for a living being, and also the name of an English island county.

clue.text: After bursting into part of a house, it cascades down

indicators.note: going into something puts these letters inside it
something bursting flies apart, so its letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: the letters of this word rearranged
a wall is part of a house

explanation.surface: Once a burst pipe floods part of a house, water pours downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a time word, but it is the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterfall is a stream dropping over a cliff or ledge, cascading down in a sheet or torrent.

clue.text: Grim start for grandad and one of his daughters

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the first letter of this word
a grandfather's daughter is a parent's sister, an aunt to the grandchildren

explanation.surface: A family gathering gets off to a bleak start for Grandad and his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: From the grandchildren's view, any of grandad's daughters other than their mother is an aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaunt can mean grim, stark and forbidding, as a gaunt landscape or a gaunt face looks bleak.

clue.text: Amusing way of catching trout

definitions.meaning: second meaning: stroking a fish's underside by hand until it can be flipped out of the water

explanation.surface: A funny method of landing a trout.
explanation.walkthrough: Trout tickling is an old poacher's technique: the fish, stroked gently from below, goes still and can be grabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickling means diverting or entertaining, and is also the name of a bare-hand fishing technique for trout.

clue.text: No strings attached if he works in gloves?

definitions.text: No strings attached if he works in gloves?

parts.note: surface reading: a deal with no conditions, as a jobbing worker in gloves might want
setter's reading: a performer whose figures have no strings because they are worn on the hand

explanation.surface: A manual labourer in work gloves wants a job with no conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No strings attached' is the idiom for an unconditional offer, but here it is literal: a glove puppet has no strings, unlike a marionette.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove-puppet operator is a performer who animates figures by hand, with no marionette strings involved.

clue.text: Entreaty made by the French in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is held inside it

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French appeal is lodged in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request, and a plea is an urgent appeal for help or mercy.

clue.text: Rule in Spain — not one I broke — caused this war

definitions.note: adjective: the name the war took

indicators.note: something broken comes apart, and its letters are reassembled in a new order
not means without, so a single I is dropped from the words before

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Napoleon's rule over Spain broke down and caused a war.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peninsular War of 1808 to 1814 was fought in Spain and Portugal after Napoleon put his brother on the Spanish throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The Napoleonic campaign on the Iberian Peninsula is known as the Peninsular War.

clue.text: Dine out on victory day, this being in the salad

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of this word rearranged
VE Day was Victory in Europe Day, 8 May 1945

explanation.surface: Diners celebrate VE Day with a meal out, and this leaf is in the salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dine out' reads as eating at a restaurant, but out is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a bitter leafy vegetable of the chicory family, commonly served raw as a salad green.

clue.text: Specialized knowledge gained by its reconstruction in a river

indicators.note: a reconstruction rebuilds something in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the letters go in the river, enclosed by it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
per means by, as in per post
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: Know-how was acquired by rebuilding something within a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe flows through Exeter in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is the specialist skill or knowledge of an expert in a particular field.

clue.text: Nasty piece of work with dynamite early in the year

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person
HE is short for high explosive, which dynamite is

explanation.surface: A villain armed with explosives strikes at the start of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: Rathe is a rare poetic word, kept in 'the rathe primrose' of Milton's Lycidas.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an archaic adjective for early-blooming or coming soon in the season, as spring flowers do.

clue.text: Once hurt badly by knight's cudgel

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and jumbled, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight's club has once badly injured someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short thick club, the sort a British policeman carried, so it is a type of cudgel.

clue.text: Over-imbibed on return to the storehouse

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol to excess

explanation.surface: Someone drank too much on the journey home to the warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Tope is an old word for drinking heavily, which a toper does.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a building where goods or supplies are kept, which is what a storehouse is.

clue.text: Cause agitation, as did Tweedledee by spoiling Tweedledum's

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to unsettle or fluster someone

definitions.note: a possessive standing for a noun: the clue names the object by its owner, fair because Tweedledum's rattle is the famous one in the rhyme
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in Through the Looking-Glass, Tweedledee spoils his brother's nice new toy, which starts their quarrel

explanation.surface: Tweedledee upset his brother by breaking his belongings, as in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme says Tweedledee had spoiled Tweedledum's nice new rattle, so spoiling it is exactly how he rattled him.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unnerve them, and a rattle is the baby's noisy toy at the centre of the Tweedle brothers' battle.

clue.text: A Continental one set down poetry for all mankind

parts.note: un is French for a
the Roman numeral for one
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A European writes down poems meant for the whole human race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' means from mainland Europe, so 'a Continental' is the French indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Universe can mean the whole world or everyone in it, as in the entire human race.

clue.text: I am introducing stuff of little account

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of these two words
stuff and material are synonyms, as cloth or matter

explanation.surface: Someone presents material they admit is trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Immaterial means unimportant or irrelevant, of no consequence to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Being free, take car to Japanese drama and Sumo wrestling

indicators.note: wrestlers twist and grapple, so the word beside it is tangled into a new order

parts.note: auto is a car
No, or Noh, is classical Japanese masked drama
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A free spirit drives off to see Japanese theatre and a sumo bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Autonomous means self-governing and independent, not ruled by anyone else.

clue.text: The way to send baggage?

parts.note: surface reading: the method by which luggage might be dispatched, perhaps by rail or post
setter's reading: way is a route, a main highway named after a large travelling chest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' reads as method but means a road; a trunk is a big luggage box, and trunk roads are Britain's main highways.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunk road is a principal highway for long-distance traffic, named as the main stem of a road network.

clue.text: Muscovite cut short the prophet

indicators.note: cutting something short trims off its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Micah is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A Russian from Moscow interrupts the prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: Muscovite looks like a person from Moscow; it is also the name of a common mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscovite is the commonest form of mica, a shiny silicate mineral that splits into thin sheets.

clue.text: Servicemen sick in the bloody channel

indicators.note: one thing set in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: an artery is a channel carrying blood
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Soldiers fall ill in a filthy canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' looks like a British swear word, but it is literal: the channel carries blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The artillery is the branch of an army made up of gunners, so the word stands for those servicemen collectively.

clue.text: One has to look below this star for illumination

definitions.text: One has to look below this star for illumination

parts.note: surface reading: a heavenly body that gives light, which an astronomer might look at
setter's reading: a printed mark that sends a reader down the page to a footnote that explains

explanation.walkthrough: The star is a printed symbol, and the illumination is the explanatory note at the foot of the page; the word comes from Greek for little star.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the star-shaped symbol in text that refers readers to a note further down the page.

clue.text: William Cantuar's double in retreat

indicators.note: a retreating army goes back the way it came, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: dual means double, twofold

explanation.surface: An archbishop's lookalike has withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Cantuar is the Latin signature of the Archbishop of Canterbury; William Laud held the post under Charles I.
explanation.definitionFit: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1633, so he signed himself William Cantuar.

clue.text: Chivvying of woman rejected by people in street

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so this name is read backwards

parts.note: a woman's name

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
men are people

explanation.surface: A spurned woman is pestered by people out in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman' stands for a girl's name, a common crossword habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivvying is nagging and pestering someone persistently, which is a form of harassment.

clue.text: Boy doubles as a signaller in Africa

parts.note: a boy's name
the boy's name is repeated

explanation.surface: A boy doubles as a signaller somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a hand-beaten drum, traditionally used to send messages across distances by sound.

clue.text: Assume control and move to the next line

definitions.meaning: first meaning: seize charge of something
second meaning: a printer's term for carrying words over onto the following line

explanation.surface: Someone seizes command and then advances to the next line of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is typesetting jargon: words that do not fit are taken over to the next line.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both gaining command of something and, in printing, shifting text down onto the following line.

clue.text: Salute a son in a wee dram

indicators.note: one thing set in another is held inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written

explanation.surface: A father raises a small whisky to his son.
explanation.walkthrough: A wee dram is Scottish for a small whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast someone is to salute them by raising a glass and drinking in their honour.

clue.text: Basil's book?

parts.note: surface reading: a book belonging to a man called Basil
setter's reading: a book about plants such as basil, the kitchen herb

explanation.walkthrough: Basil looks like a man's name with a capital B, but it is the herb, and the book is one that describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal is an old book describing plants and their medicinal or culinary uses, basil among them.

clue.text: It is most desirable to cage a wild animal

indicators.note: a cage closes round what it holds, so these letters surround the next one

parts.note: best is most desirable
taken as written

explanation.surface: Keeping a wild creature behind bars is thought the best course.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is an animal, especially a large or dangerous four-legged one living untamed.

clue.text: The goddess of islands

wordplay.note: Is is the abbreviation for island, and two of them make the plural

explanation.surface: A deity who rules over islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Isis is also the name of the River Thames as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the chief goddess of ancient Egypt, wife of Osiris and mother of Horus.

clue.text: Concerning a trial of strength

parts.note: taken as written
a bout is a contest, such as a boxing or wrestling match

explanation.surface: Something to do with a test of who is strongest.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerning and about are synonymous prepositions, both meaning on the subject of.

clue.text: Encourage one Greek leader entering ceremonially

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so these letters sit within the next phrase

parts.note: in state means with full ceremony, as a body lies in state

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of this word
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Greek chief is urged to make a grand formal entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to provoke or urge something on, so it is a stronger form of encouraging.

clue.text: Ill-timed strikes initially disrupted their corn-grinding

definitions.note: a description: what the answer did

indicators.note: disrupted things are thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter only of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: Badly timed industrial action halted the millers' grinding of corn.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the answer names mills that ground corn, so the clue says what their work was.
explanation.definitionFit: Tide-mills were waterwheel mills driven by the ebb of tidal water, used chiefly for grinding grain into flour.

clue.text: Pool made by cat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shared fund of money, as in a card game
second meaning: a pet name for a cat

explanation.surface: A pond dug by a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a communal fund players pay into, and also an affectionate word for a little feline.
